subject: Draft: Commitment sprint & acceptance criteria — Gridly Health
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@gridlyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: Commitment sprint & acceptance criteria — Gridly Health

Hi Emily,

Thanks for the conversation today. As promised, attached is a first-pass commitment sprint (MAP) that lays out the evaluation plan, acceptance tests, and an escape-hatch for the most likely blockers. This is intentionally concise so we can iterate quickly. High-level:

- Sprint: 4 weeks (trial integration + load exercise + acceptance run)
- Owners: Gridly (integration + clinical signoff), Redwood (runtime, SLOs, security evidence)
- Acceptance focus areas: latency & throughput, functional correctness on high-risk prompts, data retention controls, incident & rollback triggers

I included a short action table (tab: commitments) and a minimal test catalog (tab: acceptance_tests). Please review the acceptance tests section — key asks are:

1) Acceptance gates (must pass all):
  - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 600ms for 1k concurrent inference threads (post-integration test)
  - Throughput: sustain 500 reqs/min with <10% error rate over a 15-minute window
  - Relevance: Top-1 response precision >= 85% on the shared clinical prompt set (we'll provide scoring rubric)
  - Security: proof of data isolation (signed POA) and KMS audit logs for all requests during trial

2) Exit gates (conditions that allow pause/rollback):
  - Any P1 data exposure event OR
  - Relevance regression > 10% vs baseline on same prompt set OR
  - Latency spikes > 2x baseline sustained for >30 minutes

3) Breakglass: temporary fallback to smaller model variant + rate-limiting if GPU pool exhausted; requires immediate notification and a 4-hour incident resolution SLA from Redwood ops for trial burst events.

Attachments: gridly-map-v1.xlsx (action table + test catalog). I also added a short smoke suite (redwood-eval-tests-smoke.yaml) that we can run in your staging environment.

Next steps: can you confirm the owners in column B of the sheet and flag anything you want us to tighten/loosen? If Gridly wants a shorter sprint (2 weeks), we can compress but must cut the load exercise and replace with a synthetic stress run.

Thanks —
Naomi

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@gridlyhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@gridlyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Commitment sprint & acceptance criteria — Gridly Health

Thanks Naomi — quick read-through, this looks promising. A few clarifying Qs before we lock:

1) Data retention / logs: when you say "KMS audit logs for all requests during trial" can you confirm: does Redwood retain request payloads during hosted evaluation? What retention window and export format do you support? We need this documented for our compliance team.

2) Relevance scoring: Emily (Gridly clinical lead) will sample 200 prompts across real cases. Will Redwood run the scoring or do we provide labels? We prefer Gridly to own labeling but need your scoring pipeline to be reproducible.

3) Breakglass: can we add an additional clause that if fallback increases Latency > 30% for critical endpoints, Gridly can pause traffic immediately? Also request that Redwood provides a 2-hour bridge call window for any breakglass event.

Also attaching a short internal note: our procurement wants an estimated monthly $ impact if the trial extends beyond the sprint. Not urgent but helpful.

If you want, Tom and I can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the owners table.

Best,
Emily

Subject: Re: Draft: Commitment sprint & acceptance criteria — Gridly Health

Nice draft Naomi — added a few pragmatic tweaks below (copying Karthik for infra/quant guidance):

- Latency: propose p95 < 500ms for the staged canary test and p95 < 600ms for wide-trial. We should set the canary to run at traffic scale ~5% of expected production to validate caching behavior.
- Functional tests: split the "relevance" metric into two checks: semantic precision (top-1 precision >= 85%) and hallucination rate < 3% measured on the curated clinical probe set. We'll include a simple checklist for how to label hallucinations (see attached redwood-eval-tests-smoke.yaml).
- Smoke tests + automation: require that the smoke suite be runnable by Gridly via a single command (we will provide a tiny test harness).
- Canary rollback policy: automatic rollback if error rate > 5% for 5 consecutive minutes or any security gate triggers.

Karthik — for the breakglass: what are realistic remediation SLOs if we need to reprovision capacity or target quantized variant? Can we commit to a 4-hour remediation window for trial bursts and 24-hour fix window for deeper infra issues?

I'll merge these into v1.1 and add a two-column owner list (Redwood action / Gridly action) so it's clear.

- Ben

Subject: Re: Draft: Commitment sprint & acceptance criteria — Gridly Health (v1.1)

Emily / Tom — thanks for the quick feedback. Attached is v1.1 of the MAP (gridly-map-v1.xlsx) and the smoke suite. Key updates:

- Data retention: Redwood will NOT retain unredacted request payloads after the trial. For trial telemetry we will record request metadata + deterministic hashes of inputs so Gridly can reproduce scoring but raw PHI will not be stored. KMS audit logs will be exported as CSV for your compliance team within 24 hours of request.
- Scoring: Gridly will own label generation; Redwood will run the scoring pipeline with the exact commit used during the trial and provide the scoring notebook. We included a reproducibility checklist in the Drive link.
- Breakglass / remediation: agreed to 4-hour remediation SLA for trial capacity bursts (temporary reprovision / variant routing) and 24-hour fix window for infra bugs. Gridly can pause traffic immediately; we require a short post-mortem within 48 hours if a gate triggered.
- Acceptance tests (condensed):
  * Latency (canary): p95 < 500ms at 5% traffic for 1 hour
  * Latency (wide): p95 < 600ms across staged run (15m windows)
  * Throughput: sustain 500 reqs/min, <10% errors
  * Relevance: top-1 precision >= 85% on curated set; hallucination rate <3%
  * Security: KMS audit CSV export + signed POA for data isolation

Attachments: gridly-map-v1.xlsx, redwood-eval-tests-smoke.yaml, sla-proposal-gridly.pdf

Please reply with a single-line signoff from Gridly ("Gridly: signoff v1.1") if you accept. If you prefer a short call, Tom and I are free tomorrow 10–10:30 PT.

Once we have signoff, we'll schedule the 4-week sprint kickoff and lock deployment windows.

Thanks —
Naomi
